usageNotes: Use this to create or update a static IP-to-MAC or IP-to-VMID mapping within a VNet's IPAM table — required when a VM needs a predictable address in an SDN zone that uses IPAM (e.g. PVE IPAM or Netbox). The caller must hold SDN.Allocate on the specific zone/vnet path; supply either mac or vmid (or both) to anchor the mapping to a specific guest. Changes take effect immediately without a cluster-wide SDN apply, but the VNet and zone must already exist.

examples.summary: Pin 10.10.20.50 to a VM's MAC address inside vnet 'vl20' in zone 'sdnz01'

tips: Either mac or vmid is sufficient to anchor the mapping, but providing both avoids ambiguity when the same MAC could appear on multiple VMs (e.g. after a clone).
This endpoint returns null on success — check HTTP 200 as your confirmation; no UPID is issued.
The vnet identifier is 2–8 alphanumeric characters starting with a letter — the same constraint applies to zone.
If the IP is already mapped to a different MAC/VMID, this call overwrites the existing entry silently; verify the current mapping first with the corresponding GET if idempotency matters.
